title: Grateful Dead Live at Dupont Gymnasium M.I.T. on 1970-05-07
lineage: AudMC > ? > 7 inch Reel > DAT > HD > Soundforge > SHN

ai_review.summary: A legendary 1970 three‑set show with a monster Lovelight and stellar jams, captured on a lo‑fi audience tape that’s rough around the edges.
ai_review.review: Despite the hiss, muffled instrument separation and occasional drop‑outs typical of an early‑70s AUD, the performance shines. The acoustic set, NRPS cameo (Jerry’s steel guitar), and especially the electric second set – highlighted by a blistering Good Lovin', a soaring Easy Wind and a 31‑minute Lovelight – make this recording a must‑listen for Deadheads. Sound quality is fair at best, but the musical moments more than compensate.

ai_rating.rationale: The overwhelming majority of reviewers praise the music (many 4‑5 stars) while acknowledging the poor to fair audio quality; weighted scoring yields a strong overall rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Hissy, muffled instrument isolation and occasional drop‑outs make the tape hard to follow at times, but vocals remain intelligible and the overall ambience is present.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Three‑set marathon (acoustic, NRPS, electric) flows naturally; the acoustic and NRPS portions set a relaxed tone before the electric second set erupts with high energy and extended jams.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s shredding solo on Good Lovin' and his steel‑guitar work with NRPS receive repeated praise; his playing is described as flexible, ballsy and a highlight of the night.
